Gravely ill, the Prophet curses Jews and Christians for making prophets' graves places of worship, is nursed in Aisha's house, and has Abu Bakr lead the prayer despite Aisha's objection.
Ali refuses Abbas's urging to ask the ailing Prophet about the Caliphate; the Prophet smiles at the Muslims praying Fajr, and dies in Aisha's house after using a siwak.
Abu Bakr kisses the dead Prophet, then tells the people that Muhammad is dead but Allah lives, reciting verse 3:144, and Umar collapses on hearing it.
Those who forced medicine on him are made to take it; Aisha denies he willed the rule to Ali; he left only a mule, weapons and land; Fatima grieves.
The Prophet spent ten years in Mecca receiving the Quran and ten in Medina, died aged sixty-three, and at his death his armor was mortgaged to a Jew for barley.
When people criticise Usama's command of the troops, the Prophet says they criticised his father Zaid's before, Zaid deserved it, and Usama is among those dearest to him.
Abu al-Khair, emigrating from Yemen, hears the Prophet was buried five days before, and learns Bilal said the Night of Qadr is one of seven nights in the last ten.
Companions count the Prophet's Ghazawat: Zaid bin Arqam says nineteen, of which he joined seventeen, while al-Bara fought fifteen and Buraida sixteen with him.
Al-Fatiha, the seven oft-repeated verses, is the greatest surah of the Quran, and whoever says Ameen when the imam ends it, in time with the angels, is forgiven.
On the Day of Resurrection believers ask Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus to intercede; all decline; the Prophet intercedes until only those the Quran confines remain in Hell.
The greatest sins are setting up a rival to Allah, killing one's son for fear he will share one's food, and adultery with a neighbour's wife.
The Kam'a fungus is like manna, and its water is a cure for eye trouble.
Told to enter the gate prostrating and saying 'Hittatun', the Children of Israel entered dragging themselves on their buttocks and added 'a grain in a hair'.
Abdullah bin Salam asks the Prophet three questions only a prophet knows, embraces Islam, and the Jews, who had called him their best, then disparage him.
Umar calls Ubai the best reciter yet leaves some of his statements, since Ubai keeps all he heard though Allah says He abrogates verses or causes them to be forgotten.
Allah says the son of Adam lies against Him by denying He can recreate him, and abuses Him by claiming He has offspring, though He has no wife or child.
Umar says his Lord agreed with him in three things: the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, veiling the Prophet's wives, and warning them of better wives.
The Prophet tells Aisha the Ka'bah was not built on all Abraham's foundations, and he would rebuild it were her people not so recently out of heathenism.
As the People of the Scripture read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic, the Prophet says neither believe nor disbelieve them but declare belief in Allah's revelation.
After praying towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months the Prophet faces the Ka'bah; others turn while bowing; Allah reveals the prayers of those who died before are not lost.
On the Day of Resurrection Noah says he conveyed the Message, his nation denies it, and the Prophet's followers testify for him, as the verse on a just nation describes.
People praying Fajr at Quba hear the Prophet has been ordered to face the Ka'bah and turn to it from Jerusalem; Anas is the last left who prayed towards both.
Aisha corrects Urwa's reading of the verse on Safa and Marwa: it came because Ansar held going between them sinful; Anas says they had dropped it as pre-Islamic.
The Prophet says whoever dies invoking a rival to Allah enters Hell, and Ibn Mas'ud adds that whoever dies without doing so enters Paradise.
Unlike the Children of Israel, Muslims may take blood money instead of retribution, a mercy; for a girl's broken tooth the Prophet rules retribution until her family forgives.
People fasted on Ashura before Islam and the Prophet ordered it in Medina, but once fasting in Ramadan was prescribed, fasting on Ashura became optional.
Ibn Abbas said the verse allowing feeding a poor person instead of fasting still applies to the old who cannot fast; Ibn Umar and Salama said it was abrogated.
When Ramadan was prescribed some men broke the abstention from their wives and Allah forgave them; the white and black threads were explained as day and night, not real threads.
In the pre-Islamic period people in ihram entered their houses from the back, so Allah revealed that righteousness is fearing Allah, and to enter houses by their doors.
During Ibn az-Zubair's strife, Ibn Umar refused to shed his brother's blood, saying the command to fight until there is no affliction was fulfilled in the Prophet's time.
Hudhaifa said the verse about spending and not throwing oneself into destruction was revealed concerning spending in Allah's Cause.
Verses of Hajj explained: the ransom for shaving the head when lice troubled Ka'b bin Ujra, Hajj at-Tamattu, trading in the Hajj season, and departing from Arafat with the people.
The Prophet used to ask Allah for good in this world and in the Hereafter and to be saved from the torment of the Fire.
The Prophet said the most hated man in Allah's sight is the most quarrelsome.
Ibn Abbas read 'kudhibu' in the verse on messengers losing hope, but Aisha read 'kudh-dhibu', saying the messengers feared their followers would call them liars, never doubting Allah's promise.
On 'your wives are a tilth', Ibn Umar spoke of how a man may approach his wife; Jabir said it answered a Jewish saying about intercourse from the back.
When Ma'qil bin Yasar refused to let his divorced sister remarry her former husband after her waiting period, the verse forbidding such prevention was revealed.
Uthman would not remove a widows' verse said to be abrogated; the widow's four months and ten days, her year's bequest of residence, and a pregnant widow's term are explained.
On the day of the Trench the Prophet said the pagans had kept them from the middle prayer till sunset; the verse on guarding the prayers ended speaking in prayer.
In the fear prayer the imam leads each of two groups in one rak'a while the other faces the enemy; in great fear people may pray standing or riding.
